speaker: Doctor
text: To begin our assessment, have you noticed any new skin lesions, or are you concerned about changes in a pre-existing spot? Additionally, have you experienced any itching, bleeding, or rapid growth in these areas?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of heavy smoking and unsuccessful treatments for syphilis and eczema, I need to rule out malignancy. Have these lesions appeared suddenly, or have they been slowly progressing over months or years? Also, have you noticed any ulceration, bleeding, or pain when touched?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Liver Function Tests, and Serum Vitamin A/D levels.
REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide high-resolution photographs of the penile and digital lesions, highlighting any borders, color variations, or crusting.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (penile and digital). The combination of heavy smoking, chronic non-healing crusty lesions, location (penile shaft and digit), and prior failed treatments for eczema/syphilis strongly suggests cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. I recommend immediate excisional biopsy of both lesions for histopathological confirmation.
